_about: Quizzes written here replace a lesson's Ghost quiz. Types: choice (choices + answer index), blank (q with ____, words, answer), order (items in the right order), match (pairs). Every question has a why. draft: true means not reviewed yet.

questions.q: Byzantine worship grew from the way Christians prayed in Antioch.
questions.why: True! The Catholic Encyclopedia says it “is derived from that of Antioch.”

questions.q: What do Byzantine Catholics and Roman Catholics share?
questions.why: We share one faith and the same seven sacraments. We just pray in different ways (CCC 1202).

questions.q: “It was in ____ that the disciples were first called Christians.”
questions.why: Acts 11:26. Christians got their name in the city of Antioch.

questions.q: The Catholic Church is only the Roman, or Latin, Church.
questions.why: False! The Catholic Church is a family of Churches, Eastern and Western (Christ – Our Pascha 285).

questions.q: Who are all the Catholic Churches united with?
choices: The Pope, who takes Saint Peter’s place
questions.why: All the Catholic Churches are united with the Pope, “the successor of the apostle Peter” (Christ – Our Pascha 291).

questions.q: Where does the word “Byzantine” come from?
choices: The city of Byzantium, named for Byzas
questions.why: The city was “naturally called Byzantion” after Byzas, its founder.

questions.q: “Byzantine” is a way of praying that many different peoples share.
questions.why: True! Greeks, Slavs, Arabs and others pray the Byzantine liturgy, which spread from Constantinople.

questions.q: Byzantium was renamed ____, after Emperor Constantine.
questions.why: Constantine made it his capital, and the city took his name: Constantinople.

questions.q: What did Byzantine Catholics keep?
choices: Their Byzantine prayers, and unity with Rome
questions.why: They kept their Byzantine way of praying and stayed in communion with the Church of Rome.

questions.q: Byzantine Catholics and Orthodox Christians pray the same Byzantine liturgy.
questions.why: True! The difference is unity with the Pope. The Catechism says our communion “lacks little to attain the fullness” (CCC 838).

questions.q: What is the wall of icons called?
questions.why: The iconostasis is a wall of icons that separates and unites the sanctuary and the nave.

questions.q: In an icon of Mary, she points us to Jesus.
questions.why: True! The Mother of God holds Christ and points to him, showing us the way.

questions.q: The doors in the middle of the iconostasis are called the ____ Doors.
questions.why: The Royal (or Holy) Doors are in the center of the iconostasis.

questions.q: How do Byzantine Catholics receive Holy Communion?
choices: From a cup they hold themselves
questions.why: The priest gives the Body and Blood of Christ with a spoon, for the cleansing from sins.

questions.q: The Church holds all lawfully recognized rites to be of equal right and dignity.
questions.why: True! Catechism 1203: all lawful rites are “of equal right and dignity.”

questions.q: Match each one to what it is.
questions.why: Byzantine churches have a wall of icons called an iconostasis, with the Royal Doors in the middle, and Communion is given with a golden spoon.

questions.q: Why do we make the Sign of the Cross?
questions.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: the Christian “professes faith in the Most Holy Trinity.”

questions.q: Which shoulder do Byzantine Catholics touch first?
questions.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: “from the right shoulder to the left.”

questions.q: Three fingers joined stand for the Holy ____.
questions.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: joining the first three fingers is “a sign of our profession of faith in the Holy Trinity.”

questions.q: The Church holds all lawfully recognized rites to be of equal right and dignity.
questions.why: True! Catechism 1203: all lawful rites are “of equal right and dignity.”

questions.q: Put the Byzantine Sign of the Cross in order.
questions.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: “from the forehead to the breast and from the right shoulder to the left.”

questions.q: What job did Jesus give Peter?
questions.why: Luke 22:32: “you must strengthen your brothers.”

questions.q: Infallibility means the Pope always knows who will win the big game.
questions.why: False! Catechism 891: the gift is for “a doctrine pertaining to faith or morals.”

questions.q: Infallible means can't be ____.
questions.why: Infallible means unable to be wrong. Catechism 889: Jesus gave his Church “a share in his own infallibility.”

questions.q: The Pope never makes any mistakes at all.
questions.why: False! The Catholic Encyclopedia says infallibility “is not attributed to every doctrinal act of the pope.”
